acceptance: A claim helper exists: write the claim (startRun + task_started) and push; push success means the claim was won, push rejection means another worker won and this worker stands down before any builder dispatch
A test proves two workers racing the same task on a local fixture remote produce exactly one winner (the loser stands down with no builder dispatched and no duplicate state)
Single-worker behavior is preserved: one task per tick, claim-first dispatch
This change does not enable parallel execution; parallel execution stays off until a later directive authorizes it
Work lands on branch phase2/atomic-claim via PR; merge only by the orchestrator after verification
blockers: Held for morning-directive execution (2026-10-29): the orchestrator drives this task directly, not the overnight runner. The runner must not pick it up.
objective: Close the duplicate-processing gap with an atomic task claim (or equivalent concurrency guard) so two workers attempting the same task cannot both succeed. A branch-state check alone is not atomic and must not be assumed to be.
title: Phase 2: Atomic task claim
